subject: Spotlight: priorities, OKR check-in & QBR ask grid
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spotlight: priorities, OKR check-in & QBR ask grid

Team —

Quick weekly spotlight as we prep materials for next week's QBR. Kept this tight so the exec distro can scan in under two minutes. Attached are the one-pager and the raw OKR heatmap; I also included a short risk appendix.

TL;DR wins, main risks, and direct asks below. Please flag anything you want pulled into the QBR narrative.

Wins
- Hosted API latency improvements: p50 down 18% after kernel tuning (infra + runtime). Impact: better SLO headroom for tail-heavy customers.
- Early Dedicated pilot (Customer: Acme) completed two-week soak; no data-path regressions reported.
- First end-to-end caching experiment reduced token cost by ~11% on internal benchmarks.

Top risks (owner — impact — mitigation ask)
- Capacity squeeze on NVL-16 pool (soojin_lee) — risk: throughput may fall below committed rates for small set of Dedicated customers if we do not rebalance by EOW. Ask: approve temporary burst allocation from reserved pool.
- Quality regression on long-context chat (applied-ml/research) — risk: rollouts may need to be paused. Ask: allow a canary rollback window and prioritize additional eval runs (2 days).
- Compliance packaging delay for EU Private deployment (vanessa_ortiz) — risk: customer onboarding delay for two pipeline deals. Ask: sign off on outsourcing part of the audit evidence collection to partner integrator.

Direct asks (action — owner — due)
- Approve 48-hour temporary burst from reserved GPU pool to cover NVL-16 peak (soojin_lee) — due: 11/22 EOD.
- Confirm QBR narrative: do we keep Cost/unit improvement as a headline metric? (laura_bennett) — due: 11/21 noon.
- Approve external evidence collection for EU compliance (vanessa_ortiz) — due: 11/24.

Notes for QBR pack: I suggest we include a 1-slide callout on the caching pilot with a before/after cost delta and the customer-facing impact bullet (internal ops and cost). If you prefer a different highlight, say so.

Attachments: QBR_one-pager.pdf (one-page summary), OKR-heatmap.csv (raw numbers), risk-appendix.docx (detailed risk notes)

Thanks —
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Spotlight: priorities, OKR check-in & QBR ask grid

Marcus — thanks for the concise read. A couple quick clarifications and commitments from infra:

1) NVL-16 pool: I ran a fast allocation simulation this morning. We can move up to 6% reserved capacity as a temporary burst without violating other SLAs, but we should open an emergency rebalance ticket so the move is tracked. I've asked Austin to create the ticket (will share JIRA id).

2) Canary rollback: noted. Applied ML will need the 48-hour window you requested; I can greenlight that once we have the additional eval pass (I will assign a test runner today).

Small ask: Marcus, can you add a short note in the one-pager about the expected customer impact (two bullets) so the sales slide is customer-facing friendly?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
VP, Platform Operations

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:20:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Spotlight: priorities, OKR check-in & QBR ask grid

Marcus / Soojin — good summary. Two things I want called out and actioned before the QBR:

1) Capacity squeeze: elevate immediately. If the NVL-16 pool is at risk of impacting committed throughput for paying Dedicated customers, we must escalate to sales and CS to prepare customer communications. Soojin, please open the priority ticket and set P1 if the simulation shows customer violations. Share the expected timeline and any customer-facing mitigation language.

2) Forecast numbers: Marcus, please add the 2-week throughput forecast (expected qps per model class + confidence bands) into the OKR heatmap CSV and into the one-pager appendix. I want to see "if we do X this week, expected impact Y" — concrete numbers, not just percentages.

If you need a decision from me on reallocating budgeted burst capacity, tag me on the ticket and I will review immediately.

Laura
Laura Bennett
COO, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick update and next steps: 

- Soojin: appreciate the allocation simulation. Please open the emergency ticket (P1 if projected customer impact >0). Per Soojin's note, Austin will create JIRA INFRA-4521 and assign to infra-runbook. Marcus (that's me) confirmed we can seed the 48-hr burst from reserved pool; will not exceed 6%.

- Laura: added forecast numbers to OKR-heatmap.csv (see attachment) and added a short two-row appendix in the one-pager showing expected qps deltas under two scenarios (conservative / optimism).

- Vanessa: I drafted the outsourcing scope for EU evidence collection; it's in risk-appendix.docx. If you approve, I will send to the partner integrator and loop Sarah from Acme as a reference.

Other quick items:
- Customer-facing bullet added to QBR one-pager (two bullets under "Customer impact").
- JIRA: INFRA-4521 opened to track the NVL-16 rebalance. Link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INFRA-4521
- I attached the updated materials. If there are no further asks, I'll finalize the one-pager and ship the QBR pack by EOD Monday.

Attachments: QBR_one-pager.pdf, OKR-heatmap.csv, risk-appendix.docx

Marcus
